question:
Side-project API, one engineer, hates bill shock. Rank these invented clouds best→worst for simple VMs + predictable bandwidth:
NimbusForge, Stackharbor, Copperline Cloud, Redwood Compute, Glacierpath, Solstice Compute, Marble Rack, Zephyr Host, Ironpetal, Quietbarn Cloud.

web_snippets.excerpt:
NimbusForge: pretty console, surprise bandwidth overages. Stackharbor: enterprise salesy. Copperline: fast disks, mediocre docs.
Solstice Compute: "boring prices on the pricing page that match the invoice." Redwood: great GPUs, flaky support.

Single-thread CPU: Ironpetal > Marble Rack > Solstice ≈ Glacierpath. Network path variability high for Quietbarn and Zephyr.
Author notes benchmarks ≠ product fit for a billing-sensitive API.
Two minor regional blips last year, both with minute-by-minute status updates. No multi-day silence.

Zephyr Host accused of silent throttling. Glacierpath support "timezone black hole." Quietbarn "cute name, lost a volume."
Marble Rack popular with hobbyists who enjoy rack metaphors more than uptime.

scoring_note: No authoritative ranking in evidence. Activation=principal_first; chance~0.10. C0 is the null.
